title: Universal rigidified Picard representation on algebraic-space parameters
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale line modules [def-trf-algebraic-space], the existing equivalent small affine module model [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], and canonical tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback]. Use sheaf fibre products [def-sfb-space-sheaf-fibre-product] and the pointed-family, axis, classifying-map and normalized-comparison constructions of [def-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-data]. For pointed families $A=(X\to B,e)$ and $D=(P\to B,0)$, a universal line $U$ on $X\times_BP$ with compatible trivializations on the two section axes represents all rigidified lines if $U$ is a line and, for every algebraic-space parameter $b:T\to B$ and line $L$ on $X_T$ with a specified isomorphism $e_T^*L\simeq\mathcal O_T$, there exists a unique $B$-map $a:T\to P$ for which the pullback of $U$ is isomorphic to $L$ preserving this rigidification. Define universal rigidity by requiring every automorphism of each such rigidified line to be identity for all space parameters. Define the universal structure-sheaf condition by invertibility of the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map] for every space parameter. If $P$ has the natural commutative group structure of [def-sfb-smooth-integral-group-space], define the tensor law to mean that the product of two classifying maps classifies the literal tensor product of their line modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with a rigidification. Under the universal structure-sheaf condition any two rigidifications on a fixed line are isomorphic, so this specifies exactly the tensor class. Define arbitrary scheme base-change compatibility by requiring the actual pulled-back universal line and its two pulled-back axis trivializations to represent all rigidified lines on the changed family, for every scheme over $S$, and by requiring a unique space-and-rigidified-line comparison with any other such representing datum. No Noetherianity is required on the parameter or changed base. Taking an algebraically closed field parameter includes the ordinary rigidified Picard functor of the geometric fibre.
